title: Adaptive fidelity runbook - console demo
next_steps: Send SOC2 / ISO / KMS docs to Marcus (Redwood)
Run 3-profile perf run (INT8 / FP8 / baseline) w/ Helix dataset (Aisha)
Follow-up meeting to review results and SLAs (Jordan to schedule)
action_items: Aisha: provision sandbox + upload simple benchmark harness (due 2026-10-08)
Jordan: share pricing tiers and dedicated vs hosted cheat sheet (due 2026-10-06)
Marcus: circulate list of compliance questions (due 2026-10-07)
summary: Walkthrough of Redwood Optimize console for creating an adaptive fidelity runbook that uses INT8/FP8 profiles with fallback rules. Discussed tradeoffs between latency, cost, and fidelity, plus security and sandbox next steps.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Mills: All right good afternoon everyone? This is Jordan from Redwood, thanks for joining. Today Aisha and I will demo the Optimize console and a sample adaptive fidelity runbook.
[00:09] Liam Chen: Hey thanks — appreciate it. We got the agenda, excited to see how int eight and F P eight compare on our clinical summaries workload.
[00:18] Aisha Rao: Quick intro — I'm Aisha, solutions engineer. We'll show the console, then a short live bench, then fallback and rollout patterns. We've got about 55 minutes so we'll keep it focused.
[00:30] Priya Kapoor: Small note — we'll want to understand VPC/private deployment constraints and KMS for patient data. Marcus on security is here.
[00:38] Marcus Lee: Yep, HIPAA concerns, SOC 2, and we need audit logs for token access.
[00:43] Jordan Mills: Great, we'll call out those controls. Aisha, can you share your screen?
[00:47] Aisha Rao: Sharing now. Okay this is the Optimize console home — you've seen this briefly. First widget is the fidelity heatmap which maps latency vs response quality.
[00:58] [01:02] Aisha Rao: So here I uploaded a tiny prompt set representing Helix's clinical summary tasks. We ran three profiles: baseline fp32, int8 profile, and fp8 profile. Note: int8 gives a big CPU/GPU memory reduction, FP8 sits in the middle and sometimes gets slightly better quality on numeric-heavy outputs.
[01:20] Liam Chen: Wait when you say fp8 sometimes better — is that across all prompts or just specific edge cases?
[01:25] Aisha Rao: Good Q. It's workload dependent — for prose and long context int8 can hallucinate more, for short numeric extraction FP8 keeps fidelity better. You can see on this heatmap the x axis is median latency and y axis is quality delta vs baseline.
[01:38] [01:45] Priya Kapoor: The heatmap labels are a bit fuzzy here — is quality an automatic metric or manual scoring?
[01:50] Aisha Rao: This run used rouge and a small hand-labeled set — we also compute token-level alignment and a confidence score. The console supports uploading external evals if you want.
[02:05] Jordan Mills: To frame the decision: you can pick an aggressive int8 profile for cheaper throughput and set fallback rules to FP8 for classes of prompts where quality drops. That lets you hit cost targets while protecting key slices.
[02:18] [02:25] Marcus Lee: From security perspective, how does that work when we use Private deployment? Do the fallback rules call back to hosted endpoints outside our VPC?
[02:33] Aisha Rao: Good catch. For Private/VPC we honor routing; fallbacks can be configured to run within the same private pool or to a dedicated fallback pool. We don't route outside your network unless you enable Redwood-hosted fallback explicitly.
[02:46] Liam Chen: And KMS for model cache? We need key separation for any cached KV.
[02:51] Aisha Rao: We support customer-managed KMS/HSM in Private. KV cache items can be encrypted at rest with your keys and audit logs show access.
[03:02] [03:12] Jordan Mills: Let's walk through a sample runbook. Step one: define profiles (int8-high-throughput, fp8-balanced, baseline). Step two: define quality gates — threshold on rouge/precision for each prompt bucket. Step three: fallback rules — e.g., if rouge < 0.82 then route to fp8; if still low, escalate to baseline.
[03:30] Priya Kapoor: How do we bucket prompts? We have many templates and some user-generated free text, so buckets are noisy.
[03:36] Aisha Rao: You can bucket by prompt fingerprints, metadata (route id), or runtime classification — we ship a lightweight classifier you can run to route to a conservative profile. Fingerprinting isn't perfect but works well for templated prompts.
[03:50] [04:00] Liam Chen: I heard the term "KV cash" earlier in docs — is that K-V cache? We want clarity for our infra team.
[04:06] Aisha Rao: Sorry transcribe artifact — it's KV cache, key-value cache for transformer key/value state. It reduces repeated prefix cost for chat and multi-turn flows.
[04:15] Jordan Mills: Back to tradeoffs — INT8 typically saves 30–50% per-token cost depending on model and sequence length, but you need to validate for your test-set. FP8 often gives a better latency sweetspot with less quality loss.
[04:30] [04:40] Marcus Lee: For auditing, can we see per-request which profile was used and why it fell back? We need that in our logs.
[04:46] Aisha Rao: Yes, Optimize logs show profile id, trigger reason, confidence scores, and model variant. All of that flows into the Console's trace tab and can be exported to your SIEM.
[04:59] Liam Chen: Nice. Can we quickly run a tiny live comparison? Even just 10 samples to see delta?
[05:05] Aisha Rao: Sure, I'll kick a sandbox run. Note this is a staging environment with smaller hardware so numbers are directional.
[05:12] [05:45] Aisha Rao: Running int8 profile now — launched 10 requests. The console shows stream of per-request latency and rouge delta. Request 3 has a flag: rouge=0.71, threshold=0.82, auto-fallback to FP8 triggered.
[05:58] Priya Kapoor: That fallback latency looks good — how long is the overall penalty when it falls back?
[06:04] Aisha Rao: Depending on your infra it's a per-request extra 60–180ms if the fallback runs in the same pool. If fallback hits a cold pool or cross-region, add a few 100ms. You can reduce this by pre-warming or using a warm fallback pool.
[06:20] [06:30] Jordan Mills: Important ops point — you can configure graceful degradation: serve a short summary when FP8 still fails and route the full baseline to async re-ranking.
[06:40] Liam Chen: Hmm I like async re-rank — could be a good UX pattern for results where immediate answer isn't critical.
[06:46] Aisha Rao: Exactly. We also have confidence-based hedging — show a lower-confidence badge to users.
[06:52] [07:05] Priya Kapoor: On the bench results, can we export the raw per-prompt scores? We want to run our own stats.
[07:10] Aisha Rao: Absolutely — CSV/Parquet export included with run metadata and response tokens.
[07:17] Marcus Lee: For compliance, will the exported artifacts include PII? We need to ensure redaction for logs.
[07:23] Aisha Rao: You control what gets exported. We have a redaction step during export and allow sample scrubbing — or you can enable no-export by policy.
[07:33] [08:00] Jordan Mills: Quick question from the product side — Ana, any particular success criteria for rollouts?
[08:07] Ana Gomez: We care about median latency under 250ms for search, fidelity drop under 3% on NPS-style prompts, and overall cost per 1M requests reduction by at least 25%.
[08:17] Aisha Rao: Good. So a recommended plan: start with FP8 balanced profile in canary for 5% traffic, monitor labeled quality and token-level drift for 2 days, then expand to 25% with auto-fallback to baseline for critical buckets.
[08:32] [08:45] Liam Chen: About canary and traffic control — does Redwood integrate with our deployment pipelines? We use Spinnaker and ArgoCD.
[08:52] Aisha Rao: Integrations are via API/webhooks: you can automate profile toggles via the Redwood API. We also have Terraform-style manifests for Dedicated and Private deployment configs.
[08:58] Priya Kapoor: Nice. Any differences in quantization behavior on different GPUs? We use A100s in prod but sandbox uses slightly older cards.
[09:05] Aisha Rao: Kernel selection matters. Our runtime chooses optimized kernels per GPU and will prefer different int8/FP8 codepaths. FP8 often benefits more on newer Ampere or Hopper parts; we surface a compatibility matrix in the model catalog.
[09:18] [09:30] Marcus Lee: If we do a dedicated pool, what's the SLA for a fallback if primary profile is saturated?
[09:36] Jordan Mills: For Dedicated we provide SLA-backed latency percentiles; fallback to a burst pool is configurable. We'll include expected failover latencies in the contract.
[09:44] Liam Chen: Can we tag requests with customer metadata for cost allocation per product team?
[09:50] Aisha Rao: Yes — token-level cost breakdown supports route and tag metadata; billing export supports per-route cost attribution.
[09:58] [10:10] Jordan Mills: We're reaching the live run results — here's the summary CSV. For your 10-sample run: int8 median latency 140ms, avg rouge delta -0.07; FP8 median latency 170ms, avg rouge delta -0.02; baseline median 230ms. Two prompts triggered fallback to FP8.
[10:29] Priya Kapoor: Those numbers are promising. The delta on the key extraction prompts worries me though.
[10:34] Aisha Rao: That's expected — extraction often needs higher precision. We recommend conservative routing for any numeric/medication templates.
[10:42] [11:00] Marcus Lee: A security ops question — where are the logs stored and how long by default?
[11:06] Jordan Mills: Default retention is 90 days; enterprise customers can extend retention or ship logs to your S3/GCS with lifecycle rules. All logs are encrypted and access-controlled.
[11:16] Liam Chen: If we want to do a 1-week pilot with a 100k request subset, what's the onboarding timeline?
[11:21] Jordan Mills: Typical: sandbox access same day, pilot config + provisioning 2–3 business days, guided bench 1 week. So about 7–10 business days end-to-end.
[11:30] [11:45] Ana Gomez: Any specific risks you want us to watch for?
[11:49] Aisha Rao: Watch distribution shift — quant profiles are sensitive to input distribution. Also, rollouts should include an evaluation harness and labeled prompts to catch regressions.
[11:58] Liam Chen: Ok makes sense. One more on cost modeling — can we get a modeled projection for 1M requests for each profile?
[12:04] Jordan Mills: Yes we'll send a cost matrix (Jordan action item). It includes per-token estimate, expected savings, and projected latency percentiles.
[12:12] [12:30] Priya Kapoor: For Private, what's the on-prem package dependency list? We need OS, driver, and kernel versions.
[12:37] Aisha Rao: We'll share the deployment checklist; it includes driver versions, CUDA, docker runtime and an optional installer for air-gapped installs.
[12:46] Jordan Mills: Let's recap next steps. We'll provision sandbox + a small dataset (Aisha), Marcus gets security docs, Jordan will send pricing and schedule the benchmark.
[12:56] [13:10] Liam Chen: Great — thanks both. We'll review once we have the sandbox numbers.
[13:15] Jordan Mills: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links to the console recording and CSV.
[13:20] End of recording.
